name: ahk-str
goal: Build str.ahk, the campaign's pure string-helper building block (Lower, Upper, Title, Default, Coalesce): expression-mode case helpers that return new strings instead of mutating in place, and default/coalesce helpers that treat the empty string as the only empty value. Author and tester work from crew/contracts/ahk_str.md alone; acceptance is the hidden TAP test file plus the ahk scanner and API gates.

tasks.instructions: Two AutoHotkey v1.1 quirks will trip you. (1) StringLower and StringUpper are legacy COMMANDS with no return value: run them into a local variable, then return that variable; 'return StringLower(text)' silently yields the empty string, and title case is the command's third parameter T (StringLower, out, text, T), not a function call. (2) The string "0" is FALSY in v1.1: Default and Coalesce must test for the empty string explicitly (value == ""), never with 'if (value)' truthiness, or they will wrongly replace "0" and 0. Also: every line of code inside a function, no percent signs anywhere, no ByRef.
tasks.test_instructions: Write TAP tests from the contract alone: first line #Include tap.ahk, then #Include str.ahk, using only Is(got, want, name) and Ok(condition, name), ending with Done(). Is compares with == (case-sensitive), so every expected string must be exactly cased as the contract's examples show - copy them verbatim. Cover every numbered rule with at least one check: rule 3 (Title resets mixed case, does NOT capitalize after a hyphen or apostrophe: "Don't Stop", "The-end"), rule 4 ("0" and 0 are kept, never replaced), rule 6 (zero-argument Coalesce is ""), rule 10 (caller's variable unchanged after Lower/Title/Default), rule 11 (nested calls). Never assert mere non-emptiness such as Ok(x != "") - every check pins an exact expected value. No labels, no hotkeys, no percent signs.
